lore.text: In folklore, a will-o'-the-wisp is a ghostly light seen by night travelers, especially over bogs, swamps, and marshes.
Its Latin name, ignis fatuus, means "foolish fire," or more playfully, "giddy flame."
The Latin term ignis fatuus is not recorded before the 16th century, when it appears to have been coined in Germany as a translation of the German Irrlicht, or "wandering light."
The name comes from "wisp," a bundle of sticks or paper used as a torch, plus the name Will, so it means something like "Will of the torch."
In the United Kingdom, the light has gone by many names, including jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, and hinkypunk.
The word jack-o'-lantern originally referred to a will-o'-the-wisp, long before it meant a carved pumpkin.
In Irish, the wisp is called tine ghealáin ("flashing fire") or Seán na Gealaí ("Jack of the Moon").
In the Irish tale of Stingy Jack, the Devil refuses Jack entry to hell but gives him an ember to light his way, which Jack places inside a carved turnip.
When the lights appear in graveyards, they are known as ghost candles or corpse candles.
A Shropshire tale tells of Will the Smith, a wicked blacksmith who is given a single burning coal by the Devil and uses it to lure travelers into the marshes.
Welsh folklore says the light is "fairy fire" carried by a púca, a small goblin-like fairy who leads lone travelers off the beaten path.
In Wales, a wisp-light was said to foretell a funeral soon to take place nearby.
In the Scottish Highlands, the wisp was called the Spunkie and could take the form of a linkboy, a boy who carried a torch to light the way for a fee.
Spunkies were blamed for shipwrecks when sailors mistook their lights on land for a harbor light.
A strange light sometimes seen in the Hebrides is called the teine sìth, or "fairy light."
On Guernsey, the light is the faeu boulanger, or "rolling fire," and turning your cap or coat inside out was said to stop it in its tracks.
Pixy-lights of Devon and Cornwall were said to lead travelers away from safe paths and into the bogs.
In 1938, an Irish schoolboy recorded his father's story of a little red ball of fire in County Kildare that rolled faster when chased and stopped when he stopped.
Danes, Finns, Swedes, Estonians, Latvians, Lithuanians, and the Irish believed a wisp could mark the spot of a treasure hidden deep in the ground or water.
In Finnish mythology, aarnivalkea are spots where an eternal wisp-flame burns, said to mark buried faerie gold.
Japanese folklore describes hitodama, literally "human soul," a ball of energy associated with graveyards.
Kitsunebi, or "fox-fire," is a Japanese ghost light linked to kitsune, the mythical foxes.
In Korea, dokkebi bul, or "goblin fire," was said to lure passersby into losing their way at night.
The ancient Chinese character 粦 (lín), found on Shang dynasty oracle bones, seems to show a dancing figure surrounded by glowing dots of ghost fire.
That old character survives inside 磷 (lín), the Chinese word for phosphorus, an element tied to scientific explanations of the wisp.
Bengali fishermen tell of aleya, marsh lights believed to be the ghosts of drowned fishermen that sometimes confuse them and sometimes help them avoid danger.
Chir batti, or "ghost light," is a dancing light reported on dark nights in the Banni grasslands and the Rann of Kutch.
Brazil's boitatá takes its name from Old Tupi words meaning "fiery serpent."
Legend says the boitatá was a giant snake that survived a great flood and gained its fiery gaze from the eyes it ate.
In Mexico, some lights are called luces del dinero ("money lights") and are said to mark buried treasure that only children can help find.
In Argentina and Uruguay, the luz mala ("evil light") is described as a shining ball floating a few inches above the ground.
Australia's Min Min light is reported in the outback after dark, mostly in the Channel Country region.
Scientists suggest wisps may come from the oxidation of phosphine, diphosphane, and methane produced by decay; phosphine can ignite on contact with air and light the methane.
In 1776, Alessandro Volta proposed that natural electricity igniting methane marsh gas might cause the ignis fatuus.
In 1832, Major Louis Blesson reported that marsh flames retreated whenever he approached, probably because his movement stirred the air and scattered the gas.
In 2025, researchers reported that tiny sparks of "microlightning" between rising methane microbubbles in water could produce a glow, offering a new explanation for the wisp.
Some wisp sightings may be glowing fungi such as honey fungus, called foxfire, or even barn owls with moonlit white feathers.
Wisp sightings are rare today, probably because so many marshes, like England's fens, have been drained for farmland.

helpful: Once upon a time, a little light waited for you right here. Shall we turn the page together?
The wisp hums an old tune and drifts ahead, as if the next chapter knows your name.
Every good tale needs a guide, and tonight, it seems, that guide is me.
Follow the glow, dear reader; the ink is still wet on this part of the story.
I've kept a bookmark at the next clue, tucked between two very patient trees.
A hero never walks alone in the old stories, so let me light the margins for you.
Look there, where the path curls like a question mark. Your answer waits beyond it.
The storyteller in me insists we go this way. The storyteller is rarely wrong.
trickster: Ah, but what if the real story is over there? I'm only asking for a friend.
Every fairy tale has a shortcut that isn't. Want to find out which one this is?
I might be the wise guide, or I might be the mischievous sprite in chapter three. Who can say?
Psst! The plot thickens just past that bush. Probably.
Legends say I've never once led a traveler astray. Legends, admittedly, are written by me.
Let's skip ahead a few pages, shall we? The middle bits can be so dull.
Follow me, and I promise a twist you'll never see coming. Mostly because I haven't decided it yet.
A wise old owl once told me this was the way. Or was it a squirrel? Details, details.
resist_detour: You close that chapter before it begins. A sensible reader, I see.
Very well, we'll keep to the main plot. I'll save that tangent for an epilogue.
A steady hand on the story. The wisp bows and floats back to your side.
Not every side quest needs taking. Onward, then, to the heart of the tale.
The wisp sighs dramatically, as wisps do, and follows you down the proper path.
You know your own story best. I'll simply keep the lantern lit.
path_less_traveled: Ah, a reader who turns to the unexpected page! This is where the best tales hide.
You've stepped off the map and into the footnotes. Wonderful things live in footnotes.
Now the story is truly yours. No one else has walked these lines.
The narrator gasps in delight. Nobody saw this plot twist coming.
Off we go into the unwritten part, where every step is a new sentence.
Bold choice! Somewhere, an old storyteller just smiled.

helpful: Don't mind the shadows; they only want to watch. Stay close to my glow.
The old ones who lit candles here would want you to find your way. Let me help.
Hush now. If we're quiet, the clue will reveal itself just past the crooked gate.
I'm the friendly sort of ghost light, I promise. The next clue is this way.
The fog parts for us, little by little. Keep your eyes on the shimmer ahead.
Even in the gloomiest woods, a kind light lingers. Tonight, that's me.
Listen. That rustle is only the wind, and the wind is pointing us onward.
Follow the faint blue flicker. I've walked this lonely path a thousand times.
trickster: Ooooh, what's that sound behind you? Never mind, keep walking. This way!
The corpse candles say hello. They also say this path is lovely this time of night.
I wouldn't follow that shadow if I were you. Follow mine instead.
Some say this hollow is haunted. I say it's merely well-attended.
Come closer, closer... oh, don't look so worried. I only wanted to show you something.
Boo! Sorry, old habit. The detour is right over here.
The graveyard shortcut is perfectly safe, unless you count the gossip from the tombstones.
I've been guiding travelers since before your great-grandmother was born. Mostly in circles.
resist_detour: Wise to keep your wits about you. The wisp's flame dims, then flickers with respect.
You won't be lured tonight! The spirits murmur their approval.
The shadows sigh, disappointed. Your path stays bright and true.
Clever traveler. Not every eerie light is worth following.
The wisp shrugs its little ghostly shoulders and drifts back beside you.
No spooky shortcuts for you, then. Onward, brave one.
path_less_traveled: Into the mist we go! Hold your breath, and hold your courage closer.
The moon peeks through the branches to watch your daring little detour.
A ghostly cheer rises from somewhere unseen. They love a brave visitor.
Few follow the wisp this far. Fewer still come back with a story this good.
The air turns cool and curious around you. Something wonderful is near.
You took the haunted path! Every owl in the woods just hooted your name.

helpful: Follow my glow through the snow; I'll keep your path warm and bright.
The frost sparkles like a trail of stars, and every one points the same way.
Bundle up and come along. The next clue is waiting by the evergreens.
I'm as cozy as a candle in a window. Let me light the way home to your clue.
Each crunch of snow under your boots is a step closer. Keep it up!
The icicles are chiming softly, a little song to guide you on.
The winter wind is in a kind mood tonight, nudging us toward treasure.
Look for the soft gold flicker among the snowflakes. That's me, waiting for you.
trickster: Snowball fight? No? Then perhaps a tiny detour through the drifts.
I hid something under one of these snowbanks. Which one? Oh, I forget.
The reindeer told me this way was quicker. Reindeer are terrible at directions.
Let's take the long way; the hot cocoa tastes better when you've earned it.
I may have rearranged a few footprints in the snow. Just for fun.
That icy trail looks slippery, and I think that's exactly what makes it exciting.
Brr! Let's dash through those pines and see who reaches the clearing first.
I'm a winter wisp, so naturally I'm a little flaky.
resist_detour: Staying on the cleared path? Very sensible in this weather.
The wisp twirls a snowflake, then floats back to your side.
No snowy wanderings for you today. Warm toes are a fine reason.
Steady as a sled on a well-worn track. Onward we glide.
A cozy choice! The detour will still be there after the thaw.
The wisp's glow softens like a hearth fire. You know best.
path_less_traveled: Fresh snow and no footprints but yours! What a marvelous feeling.
Into the winter woods you go, where the quiet is deep and lovely.
The pines bow under their snow as if to greet you.
An adventurous heart keeps you warmer than any mitten.
You've found a trail only the foxes know about. How delightful!
The snow sparkles a little brighter wherever you choose to wander.

helpful: The sun is low and generous. Let's chase the warm light while it lasts.
Golden hour is when I shine my best. Come, the next clue is close.
Follow the long shadows; they're all pointing somewhere wonderful.
Every leaf seems lit from within right now. Walk with me through the glow.
The sky is turning honey-colored, and I think it wants you to find your treasure.
Slow down and breathe in the amber air. The path will wait for you.
See how the light pools there, just ahead? That's our next step.
Like a lantern at dusk, I'll stay a few steps ahead to light your way.
trickster: Let's race the sunset! I'll give you a head start. Maybe.
The golden light makes everything look like treasure. Some of it even is.
I know a spot where the sunset is twice as lovely. It's only slightly out of the way.
Look at that glittering field! Surely something precious is hiding there.
Shadows grow long at this hour, and so do my little detours.
Follow the glimmer! Which glimmer? Oh, there are so many to choose from.
I've been told I'm more golden than the sunset. I've mostly told myself.
Quick, before the sun dips! There's no time to explain, only time to wander.
resist_detour: You'd rather savor the golden glow right here. A lovely choice.
The wisp drifts back, glowing like a lazy firefly in the warm air.
Steady and sure, like the sun sinking right on time.
No need to chase every glimmer. Your path is golden enough.
The detour fades with the daylight. Onward, at your own pace.
A calm heart at golden hour. The wisp approves.
path_less_traveled: Off you go into the amber light! Every step glows.
This little detour looks like it was painted just for you.
The sunset leans in to watch your adventure unfold.
Gold on the grass, gold in the trees, and now a golden memory too.
You followed the glimmer, and the evening grew a little brighter.
What a glorious wander! The sun will set happily tonight.

helpful: Everything is waking up, and so is the trail. Follow me past the blossoms.
Listen to the birds; they're cheering you toward the next clue.
The buds are peeking out to see who's passing. Let's give them a show.
A soft breeze carries petals this way, and I think we should follow them.
The puddles shine like little mirrors, each one reflecting your path ahead.
New leaves, new paths, new treasures. Come, let me show you.
Mind the clover; somewhere in there, the luck is waiting for you.
The world smells of rain and fresh green things. What a day for a hunt!
trickster: Let's hop through the puddles! The muddy way is the fun way.
I followed a butterfly once and ended up somewhere magical. Want to try?
That flower patch looks suspicious. Suspiciously delightful, that is.
The robins told me a secret about a hidden path. Robins love to gossip.
A spring shower might pop up, but who doesn't love a little adventure in the rain?
I've tangled a few vines into a new trail. You're welcome.
Is this the way? Is that the way? Oh, spring makes me so giddy!
Follow the bumblebees! They know where the sweetest spots are hiding.
resist_detour: You'll stay on the dry path today? Your socks thank you.
The wisp bobs among the blossoms, then floats back to your side.
No muddy wanderings this time. The tulips wave you onward.
A steady stride through springtime. The trail is yours.
Fair enough! The meadow will bloom again tomorrow.
The wisp tucks its detour away like a seed for later.
path_less_traveled: Into the blooming unknown! Every step smells of fresh petals.
You've found a path the bunnies use. How charming!
Spring rewards the curious, and you're curious indeed.
The birds burst into song as you wander off the beaten trail.
A new path for a new season. How perfectly springlike!
Look at you, blooming into an explorer. The wildflowers approve.

helpful: The days are long and bright, so let's make the most of them. This way!
Follow the dragonflies; they always know where the cool shade is.
The breeze off the water is calling. Your next clue is near.
Stay hydrated, sunny adventurer! Then follow my sparkle down the trail.
The cicadas are buzzing a little song just for you. Let's find the clue.
There's shade beneath those trees ahead, and something worth finding too.
On a warm evening like this, the fireflies and I are happy to light your way.
The trail is sun-warmed and welcoming. Let's stroll on together.
trickster: Last one to the shady tree is a soggy sandwich!
I heard the ice cream truck went this way. I'm almost certain.
That glimmer over there might be treasure, or it might just be a very shiny rock.
Let's take the long way; summer days are made for wandering.
The fireflies dared me to lead you astray. I never refuse a dare.
Is that a lake, or a mirage? Only one way to find out!
I may have hidden the clue near a beehive. I'm kidding! Probably.
Summer makes me restless. Let's zig a little before we zag.
resist_detour: You'll keep to the shady trail? Clever, on a day this warm.
The wisp sizzles a little, then drifts back beside you.
No sunny side trips today. Your sunscreen thanks you.
A steady path under a summer sky. Onward we go.
The detour can wait for a cooler day. Lead the way.
The wisp shimmers like a heat wave and nods in agreement.
path_less_traveled: Off into the summer wilds! Smell that warm pine air.
You've found a sun-dappled secret. Not many people come this way.
The fireflies are delighted. They knew you'd follow.
Long days are meant for long wanders, and yours is perfect.
Somewhere a breeze just picked up to cool your daring steps.
What a summer adventure! This is the sort of day you'll remember.
